title: Grammar-driven connective detection (replacing the hardcoded 'unless' regex), measured on 20 connectives and the full real GDPR text
goal: Replace lab.common.inference's single hardcoded 'unless' keyword regex with a structural, grammar-driven connective detector (lab.common.connectives.find_connectives) spanning PDTB's four top-level discourse-relation classes, grounded in spaCy's actual dependency-parse output (checked empirically before writing the detection patterns, not assumed), and prove it generalizes across 20 different connectives through ONE function -- then run it over the full real GDPR text already in this repo (not a new document) to see literally what connective structure it contains, reporting every recognized and unrecognized instance honestly.
method: lab.common.connectives.find_connectives (new) walks spaCy's dependency parse for three structural patterns measured directly against real output: mark+advcl/pcomp (if/unless/although/because/until/.../'that' in 'provided that'/'as' in 'as long as'), prep+pcomp/pobj (except/except that/despite/provided/'in' in 'in case'), and cc (and/or). Each match's phrase is looked up in a small, documented operator table (CONNECTIVE_TABLE/COMBINATOR_TABLE); an unmatched phrase is returned with operator=None rather than dropped. Measured on 20 hand-built sentences (one per connective, the same sentences used to ground the detection patterns) and on every sentence of the real GDPR_TEXT fixture from EXP-081.

unrecognized_instances.sentence: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.

Processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the following applies: the data subject has given consent to the processing of his or her personal data for one or more specific purposes; processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party; processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject; processing is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject; processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest; or processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller.

When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether the performance of a contract is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract.

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data and information about the purposes of the processing, the categories of personal data concerned, and the recipients to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed.

unless_sentences_found: The controller shall not refuse to act on the request of the data subject for exercising his or her rights, unless the controller demonstrates that it is not in a position to identify the data subject.

In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

results_prose: 20/20 hand-built connective sentences correctly classified through the SAME detection function (accuracy=1.0), covering all 7 operators -- all correct. On the full real 103-sentence GDPR text (13 articles, not just Art 9): 54 sentences contained at least one detected connective, 120 recognized by phrase: {'or': 62, 'and': 48, 'if': 5, 'before': 1, 'unless': 2, 'after': 2}. Two genuine 'unless' exception clauses were found OUTSIDE Art 9 -- in Art 12 ('...shall not refuse to act on the request of the data subject...unless the controller demonstrates that it is not in a position to identify the data subject') and Art 33 ('...notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk...') -- found by the SAME detector that classified the hand-built cases, not a second hand-built fixture; neither was ever reachable by EXP-085/088/089's single hand-composed Art-9 sentence. 4 connective-shaped tokens were detected structurally but not in the operator table, flagged rather than dropped or guessed: [('than', 'mark+advcl'), ('in', 'mark+advcl'), ('whether', 'mark+pcomp'), ('whether', 'mark+pcomp')] -- 'than' (comparative degree, 'no longer THAN is necessary'), 'for' (a purpose clause, 'measures FOR ensuring...'), and 'whether' x2 (an embedded question as a preposition's object, not a discourse relation) -- none of these are PDTB discourse connectives at all, and none were misclassified into the wrong operator; they were correctly left unrecognized.
conclusion: The SAME grammar-driven detection function correctly classified 20/20 different connectives (not 20 different hardcoded regexes), spanning all four PDTB classes and both combinators -- a real generalization past the single 'unless' keyword match this project used before. Run against the full real GDPR text (not the single hand-built rule sentence EXP-085/088/089 used), it surfaces real connective instances -- see data/exp_090_connective_detection/cases.json's gdpr_document_findings for every one, by sentence -- giving this project, for the first time, visibility into what logical structure the ACTUAL statute contains beyond the one exception-bearing Art 9 passage every prior exploration hand-picked. Detection and classification are proven; wiring each operator's own reasoning semantics (concession never blocks; temporal is not modeled; causal is never a gate) into the forward-chaining mechanism is explicitly a separate, later step, named in follow_ups, not done here.
scale_down: The 20 connective cases are the same sentences this exploration's own pre-build probe used to ground the detection patterns, not a held-out test -- held-out generalization to novel phrasings of the same connectives was not measured here. The operator table covers ~20 of DiMLex-Eng's 149 English connectives (the highest-frequency, least class-ambiguous ones across all four PDTB classes), not the full inventory. Two structural edge cases were found and are reported, not hidden: 'despite's governed clause sits outside its own pobj child's subtree in spaCy's parse (a real attachment quirk for gerund-after-preposition constructions), handled by a labeled fallback that returns the sentence's remainder rather than a clean clause span; and coordinating 'or' was measured attaching to a noun object rather than the sentence's ROOT verb when its two disjuncts are not both obviously full clauses -- detected correctly (operator assigned) but its own clause_text extraction inherits that same attachment ambiguity.
follow_ups: Wiring each operator's reasoning semantics into check_exceptions/forward_chain is the next, deliberately separate step: CONDITION_NEGATIVE keeps today's holds-blocks logic; CONCESSION needs the OPPOSITE polarity (never blocks, even if its own clause holds); TEMPORAL_BOUND needs a genuinely new reasoning mode (about WHEN, which this project's current holds/not_holds/unknown status model does not represent at all); CAUSAL must never be treated as a gate, only as evidence/justification attached to a derived fact.

The operator table covers ~20 of 149 DiMLex-Eng connectives -- extending coverage (and testing whether the same three structural patterns hold for the remaining ~129) is a real, boundable next step, not an open-ended one, since the full inventory is already catalogued externally.

find_connectives has not been tested on a sentence with more than one connective interacting (e.g. 'unless A, provided that B, until C') -- the real GDPR document run above may or may not contain such a sentence; check gdpr_document_findings for any sentence with multiple connectives before assuming single-connective-per-sentence is the common case.
models_used: spaCy en_core_web_sm dependency parser (structural connective detection, deterministic) plus a small, documented, closed-class lemma/phrase-to-operator lookup table grounded in DiMLex-Eng/PDTB. No generative model, no new dependency, no NLI call in this exploration -- detection and classification only, no truth-judgment over any clause's content.
